title: The Adventure Is Not the World
description:
Tell the story of first-class adventure modules.

Narrative hook and core question: What is an adventure module in a system that can improvise indefinitely?

Write only after module architecture is implemented and exercised enough to tell the history honestly. Research why prompt injection of adventure text is insufficient; module as authored canonical spine; module schema and typed records; campaign binding; module progress state; DM runtime context; progress audit; module truth versus player-discovered knowledge; authored content versus campaign divergence; and how improvised consequences overlay authored content without rewriting the source module. Cover Ember Hollow only when the evidence and naming in the repository support it.

Expected architectural conclusion: an adventure module is authored scenario truth with campaign-owned progress and divergence, not the whole world and not a prompt pasted into context.

Boundaries: do not treat the current module epic as complete if it is not. Do not claim module UX or playtest maturity that artifacts do not support. Do not absorb the campaign-memory or rules-pack compiler story.

Use repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence. Verify claims against artifacts rather than model memory; distinguish implemented from planned architecture; preserve public readability and search indexing; and follow Joseph's voice rules: analytical and curious, concrete before abstraction, dry humor when earned, deliberate we/I attribution, reflect praise, absorb blame, no em dashes, and no generic LLM prose.
